docs.syntax: =SUM(range1, range2, ...) across separate blocks, or =SUM(B2:D4) across one rectangle
docs.explain: SUM takes as many arguments as you like, and each one can be its own block. Two quarters that sit in columns B and D are one call with a comma between them: SUM(B2:B3,D2:D3). The comma is doing the work. With no comma the two blocks become a single broken reference and the formula refuses to read. When the blocks form a rectangle, the alternative is one range across the lot. SUM(B2:D4) counts every number inside it and ignores the text in the middle and the empty cell in the corner. That is why a block total is safer than a column of subtotals. Text and blanks cannot poison it, while a chain of plus signs hits the text and returns an error. Watch for a block that includes a total row of its own. A rectangle is only too big when the extra cells are numbers, and a total row always is.

errors.text: A cell in a hand-written chain holds text; SUM over a range would have skipped it.
A division by zero in the formula stops it before a total is produced.
A block references a range that no longer exists after rows or columns were deleted.
